I couldn't do this research. My first attempt to fetch the sources (Enduring Word, and Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub for Ezekiel 47) returned no pages. Instead, the tool said I have no web calls left for this turn. So I haven't read any of the approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. I have nothing sourced to report, so I've left the notes empty rather than fill them from memory.

If you send the request again in a new turn, I'll start with these pages:

- **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-47/, plus the Bible Hub and StudyLight pages for Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and others on Ezekiel 47, and Precept Austin.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** whether the temple and river are a literal future (millennial) temple or a symbol of the gospel and the church. For one side I'd check gty.org and gotquestions.org; for the other, ligonier.org, thegospelcoalition.org and monergism.com. I'd also check what Wesleyan, Pentecostal and Lutheran sites have on the river's waters.
- **Other views:** the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship. For Catholic and Orthodox readings, I'd look at the Church Fathers on New Advent and at catholic.com and oca.org, where the water may be read as baptism.

You could also paste the text of any of those pages here, and I'll write the verse-by-verse notes from them with URLs.
